location: T-101 to T-108; 24 h storage statement
observed: Eight tanks labelled 25 MIG give 200 MIG, exactly 24 h at 200 MIGD. The drawing does not identify whether 25 MIG is usable or gross volume.
required_action: Define gross and usable storage, dead volume, minimum operating level and any reserved volume. If 25 MIG is gross, usable autonomy is less than 24 h. With one nominal 25 MIG tank unavailable, gross autonomy is 21 h; the drawing does not claim 24 h N-1, so confirm whether that is required.
closure_document: Storage calculation / design basis / PFD note

location: Three typical incoming lines upstream of the common inlet manifold
observed: Each incoming line shows a MOV, FCV and FE/FIT, but no line check valve or stated reverse-flow strategy.
required_action: Confirm actual incoming line count and network pressure combinations. Establish how backfeeding between live incoming pipelines is prevented or intentionally permitted; show check/isolation arrangements only as required by the network authority and hydraulic study. Do not assume every inlet needs an NRV.

location: MOV-101 / FCV-101 / FE-101 typical inlet control
observed: Upstream motorized isolation is shown. Local downstream isolation, FCV maintenance bypass and metering maintenance provisions are not shown.
required_action: Confirm the maintenance philosophy. Where one inlet control train must remain maintainable with the other lines live, provide suitable isolation on both sides of the equipment. A bypass is conditional, not automatically required. Check meter straight lengths, FCV cavitation/noise and valve fail/closure behavior in the P&ID and calculations.

location: LIT-101 (TYP.), tank inlet MOVs and main pumps
observed: A typical level transmitter and tank inlet/outlet MOVs are shown, but the functional high-high filling shutdown and low-low pump protection are not stated.
required_action: Add the operating philosophy: tank high-high level inhibits/closes the appropriate filling path; tank/header low level or low suction pressure prevents unsafe pump operation. Define valve proof, pump sequencing and independent protection requirements in the P&ID/cause-and-effect. Do not invent trip settings.

location: Each tank overflow and bottom drain to OP-101
observed: Side overflow and bottom drain connections join dashed lines to OP-101. Individual bottom-drain isolation is not shown.
required_action: Distinguish the normally closed, isolable bottom drain from the overflow, which must remain available. Document screened/sanitary termination, air gap or equivalent backflow protection, venting and capacity. Prevent lagoon or pit water from reaching potable storage. Do not place an ordinary shutoff valve in the required overflow path.
closure_document: PFD clarification / tank and drainage P&IDs

location: MOV-102 (NC), inlet manifold to suction header
observed: The inlet-to-suction bypass and its normally closed MOV are present. The pressure transition and mode interlocks are not described.
required_action: Define bypass mode using actual incoming pressure. Check pressure exposure of the suction system and tank outlet lines, potential reverse filling through tank outlets, NPSH, surge and isolation proof. Determine required pressure reduction, backflow protection and tank-isolation interlocks from the approved arrangement.
closure_document: Hydraulic study / PFD operating note / P&ID

location: Tank outlet manifold to three suction-header sections
observed: The normal path is correctly shown as storage to suction header to main pumps. No water levels or hydraulic-loss data establish the gravity-feed performance.
required_action: Verify the hydraulic grade and NPSH available at minimum tank level for both groups, with the intended maximum simultaneous flow and unavailable tanks/sections. Include entrance, manifold, suction-valve and pipe losses; compare against actual pump NPSH requirements and project margin.

location: P-301 to P-307 and P-311 to P-313 suction branches
observed: Discharge NRVs and isolation valves are drawn for all ten current main-pump positions. Individual suction isolation valves are not drawn.
required_action: Show one suitable suction isolation provision for each current main pump, with future-pump provisions separately identified. Retain the existing discharge sequence pump -> NRV -> isolation -> header. Add pump casing drain/vent and local pressure measurement on the P&ID; confirm valve type and hydraulic impact.

location: Group A and Group B sectioning valves; Note 2
observed: Each discharge header is sectioned, but each has one outlet on the right side. A left-hand section cannot supply that outlet when the intervening sectioning valve is closed.
required_action: Demonstrate the claim that at least half of each group remains available with any one section isolated. Provide a suitable independently isolable outlet/header arrangement, or narrow the note to the actual supported isolation cases. Check suction and discharge sections together; pump count alone does not prove an available outlet path.

location: P-308, P-314 and future second distribution group P-321
observed: Future pump bays and a future group with separate discharge/surge provision are shown. P-321 is fed from the suction header and crosses S-22 without connection, consistent with the drawing gap convention.
required_action: Identify installed versus future valves/spools, capped or blinded live tie-ins, and the future duty/standby arrangement. Preserve the separation of the future suction connection from the existing distribution discharge header.

location: FCV-401 / FCV-411 and their bypasses
observed: Both outlet FCVs have a manual-valve bypass and a downstream common MOV. Separate block valves on the two ends of the FCV leg are not drawn; bypass normal status is unstated.
required_action: If live FCV maintenance is intended, add isolation at each end of the FCV leg, leaving the bypass path available. The downstream common MOV alone cannot isolate the FCV while bypass flow continues. State NC/secured bypass status and approved manual operation; otherwise document whole-outlet shutdown maintenance.

location: VFD pumps, outlet FCVs/MOVs and main headers
observed: VFDs and flow instrumentation are present, but main suction/discharge pressure measurement and the coordinated pressure/flow operating philosophy are not shown.
required_action: Define how VFD control and outlet FCV control interact, minimum safe pump flow and valve/pump start-stop sequencing. Confirm pressure measurement, low suction/no-flow protection and MOV closure times in the P&ID/cause-and-effect/transient study. The stated 250 m and 100-160 m heads are differential heads, not complete valve or vessel design pressures.
closure_document: PFD functional note / P&ID / surge study

observed: Metering upstream of injection and sampling/analyser points downstream of injection are correctly sequenced. Sufficient chemical mixing and representative sample conditions are not established.
required_action: Confirm mixing length or mixer requirements and sample-system design for the actual analytes, especially residual chlorine. Add analyser sample isolation, conditioning and safe drain details in the P&ID. Do not infer adequate contact or mixing from schematic spacing.

location: SV-201 / SV-202 / SV-203 typical pairs
observed: Each suction section has bladder vessels behind one common water-side isolation valve. The note correctly excludes them from the compressed-air system.
required_action: Confirm individual-vessel or train maintenance isolation, safe drain/vent and manufacturer-approved precharge provisions. Prove sufficient surge protection for permitted out-of-service cases. Keep the required bidirectional hydraulic response; do not add an ordinary NRV to the vessel water connection without a deliberately engineered surge arrangement.

location: SV-401 and SV-411, Train 1 and Train 2
observed: For each group, one takeoff valve feeds Train 1, followed by a second water-line valve between Train 1 and Train 2. This isolates Train 2 alone, or both trains; it cannot isolate Train 1 while retaining Train 2.
required_action: Provide independently isolable parallel train branches, or another arrangement that demonstrably meets the required maintenance cases. Show protected normal-open status, independent air-side isolation/control, drains/vents and the remaining active surge capacity. Revalidate the arrangement by transient analysis.
closure_document: PFD topology / surge study / vendor P&ID

location: Common S-14 air main to transmission and distribution surge vessels
observed: The same common air main supplies both groups, despite their different pump head bands. Per-group or per-vessel air pressure/level controls and water-backflow safeguards are not shown.
required_action: Establish actual vessel operating/charge pressures and provide the required regulated/control branches, isolation, NRVs or equivalent water-backflow safeguards and pressure/level protection. A 250 m water head is about 24.52 bar differential; 100-160 m is about 9.81-15.69 bar. Add suction/static pressure and transient limits before selecting compressor or receiver ratings; these conversions are not setpoints.

location: C-601 / C-602, DR-601 / DR-602 to common receiver feed
observed: Oil-free duty/standby compressors, intake equipment, aftercooler/separator and dryer/filter trains are present. Separate discharge NRVs and maintenance isolation are not drawn before the trains join.
required_action: Confirm these devices within the package and show/reference the outlet isolation and non-return function so a live receiver cannot backfeed the standby/open compressor train. Verify separator/aftercooler/dryer drains and discharge destinations. Confirm air quality and dew point against the actual W-M-SS-007 requirements.

observed: Two receivers are connected to common upstream/downstream air lines. Individual isolation, pressure indication, safety relief and low-point condensate drains are not drawn.
required_action: Confirm individual service isolation and receiver safety relief/pressure indication/drainage in the vendor P&ID. Relief protection must remain effective for every permitted isolation state; ordinary maintenance valves must not defeat required vessel protection. Establish working/design pressure from the surge duty.

observed: A manual valve and capped-looking connection are drawn at the common air main. Backflow prevention and the mobile source pressure/quality limits are not stated.
required_action: Confirm a positively capped/blinded connection, isolation and suitable NRV/backflow safeguard, with approved pressure regulation and connection procedure. The mobile source must meet the required pressure and air quality; prevent uncontrolled charging or discharge toward disconnected equipment.

location: P-801 / P-802 and utility branches
observed: Duty/standby pumps each have a discharge NRV. Individual suction/discharge isolation and consumer branch isolation are not drawn.
required_action: Confirm service-pump maintenance isolation, pressure control/protection and isolation for washdown, domestic water, disinfection and cooling makeup. Retain the two existing pump NRVs. Confirm independent domestic/potable and process-service classifications with the water authority.

location: S-41 to WS-500 and service-water supply to P-703
observed: Potable-derived service water supplies the salt/chemical process and an inhibitor-containing cooling loop; hazard-appropriate backflow protection is not shown.
required_action: Provide an approved separation/backflow arrangement at the chemical pretreatment/process supply and cooling-makeup interface, and at other hazardous utility consumers. Select air gap or appropriate tested devices according to the actual hazard and authority requirements; a pump NRV alone is not complete contamination protection.
closure_document: PFD interface note / water authority / P&ID

location: HX-701 / P-702 / HX-707 closed loop
observed: A closed cooling circuit, heat-rejection interface, main pump/motor coolers and a parallel lube-oil HX are shown. Equipment quantities, heat rejection type, duties and loss-of-cooling behavior are unstated.
required_action: Define the actual primary/secondary heat-rejection arrangement and ambient design conditions, pump/motor/lube-oil heat loads, supply/return temperatures, flow and redundancy. Confirm cooling proof and temperature/low-flow protection required for the main pumps. The two HX circuits must remain hydraulically distinct where indirect exchange is intended.
closure_document: PFD equipment duties / OEM thermal design / P&ID

location: P-702 / P-703; F-704 / V-705 / X-706; cooler branches
observed: Filters, expansion/pressure vessel and inhibitor dosing are combined in one box connected by a single branch. Component piping roles and maintenance/balancing valves are not shown.
required_action: Clarify whether filtration is full-flow or side-stream; show the expansion connection and dosing injection separately. Confirm circulation/makeup pump NRVs where needed, isolations, cooler branch isolation/balancing, vents, drains and pressure/thermal relief. Define the allowable condition when an expansion-vessel connection is isolated.

location: C2 drive-OEM package and VFD units
observed: Supply and return are shown between a generic VFD cooling package and the drives. The ultimate heat sink, heat load and failure response are not identified.
required_action: State whether the OEM system rejects heat to ambient air, a dedicated chiller or another separately defined circuit. Add its required external interfaces and thermal duty; confirm flow/temperature monitoring, maintenance isolation and drive derating/trip behavior. Do not connect it to C1 or CH-501 merely to close the drawing.
closure_document: PFD interface / VFD OEM cooling design

observed: WS-500 is labelled SOFTENER SKID only. The engineer requested carbon filter / softener skid.
required_action: Revise the label to CARBON FILTER / SOFTENER SKID and identify the actual process arrangement and package boundary. Confirm treated-water chlorine/hardness quality and consumables/regeneration against the electrolyzer vendor; the revised label must match the actual supplied equipment.

location: TK-504 and CH-501; Sheet 004 Note 3
observed: No chilled-water supply/return or storage cooling interface is shown at TK-504. CH-501 and Note 3 explicitly identify softener/electrolyzer duties only.
required_action: Add a clearly marked chilled-water supply/return or dedicated storage-cooling interface/note for TK-504 as requested. Update CH-501 duty description and Note 3 if it also serves storage. Select an OEM-approved indirect cooling method (jacket/coil/external HX as applicable), rather than connecting chilled water into the chemical contents. Confirm storage temperature, compatible materials and cooling duty.
closure_document: PFD / thermal duty / vendor storage design

location: CH-501 drawn in the softened-water feed route
observed: The route from WS-500 passes through the CH-501 symbol to EL-503 as one process line. No separate chilled-water circuit is drawn.
required_action: Clarify whether this is cooled softened process water through an integrated feed-water chiller or an indirect chilled-water HX. Identify the cooled process stream and external CHWS/CHWR interfaces separately, with the required circulation/temperature control. A chilled-water plant label alone does not define the fluid circuits.

location: P-506 split to S-16 / IP-401 and S-17 / IP-411
observed: One typical dosing pump discharges to two branches without drawn independent metering or injection NRV/isolation. The receiving headers operate at different head bands.
required_action: Show independent controllable dosing duties for each header: separate dosing trains or a proven common skid with independent branch metering/control. Confirm injection check/isolation, pressure capability, required backpressure devices and dosing-pump relief to a compatible contained destination. Prevent process water reaching TK-504 or transferring between headers through chemical piping. Base dosage on each measured water flow and approved residual-control philosophy.
closure_document: PFD dosing arrangement / dosing calculations / P&ID

location: EL-503 / TK-504 / B-505 hydrogen vent
observed: A tank hydrogen vent and dilution-air blower are correctly shown. Ventilation proof, hydrogen handling at the electrolyzers and loss-of-dilution response are not defined.
required_action: Confirm the OEM hydrogen generation, dilution and vent route for both cells and storage; verify safe termination and gas accumulation avoidance. Define blower duty/standby requirements, ventilation proof/interlock and hydrogen detection where required by the actual hazard assessment. No hydrogen limits, air rates or area classification can be selected from this PFD alone.
closure_document: PFD functional note / OEM design / hazard assessment

location: TK-505 HCl / TK-504 NaOCl / UB-501 / CS-821
observed: Bund drainage is represented as one stream to one chemical containment item. Separate acid and hypochlorite spill paths are not demonstrated.
required_action: Show physically segregated HCl and hypochlorite containment/drain paths or a specifically engineered compatible arrangement. Mixing acid and hypochlorite can release chlorine gas. State normally closed controlled bund-drain operation and identify sampling/collection/disposal; do not route both uncontrolled spill streams to one common sump.
closure_document: PFD segregation / chemical drainage P&ID / containment design

observed: Carbon/softener backwash or regeneration waste, brine/process reject and acid-cleaning effluent destinations are not identified.
required_action: Identify the actual waste streams, quantities and compatible containment/treatment destinations. Show the cleaning transfer/flush function and containment of acid-cleaning effluent. Distinguish brine, acid, hypochlorite and ordinary washdown; the exact package valving belongs in its P&ID.
closure_document: PFD waste interfaces / vendor P&ID / treatment design

location: P-811 / P-812 discharge to TK-831
observed: Two submersible pumps join a common discharge without drawn individual NRVs or discharge isolation.
required_action: Confirm an individual discharge NRV and service isolation for each sump pump so the duty pump cannot send water through the standby pump into the pit. Add level-based duty/standby controls, high-high alarm and usable sump/holding volumes in the P&ID and drainage calculations.

location: Typical header drain valve to TK-831
observed: One typical drain takeoff is shown on the Group B discharge, with a connection to the drainage holding tank. Complete isolated-section drains and controlled depressurization are not demonstrated.
required_action: Provide the necessary low-point drains and high-point venting for suction/discharge and isolated sections, based on the actual pipe profile. Establish safe staged pressure letdown, receiving-tank venting and energy dissipation for high-pressure discharge-header drainage. Avoid an uncontrolled pressurized connection into a civil holding tank.
closure_document: PFD drain note / P&ID / depressurization calculation

location: TK-504 bottom drain to LG-102 labelled HYPERCHLORINATION DRAINAGE
observed: The chemical storage tank bottom drain goes directly to the hyperchlorination-water lagoon route. Product-drain concentration and lagoon suitability are not stated.
required_action: Distinguish stock hypochlorite product drains from chlorinated pipeline/disinfection wash water. Route concentrated product to a compatible contained collection/treatment system, or explicitly prove LG-102 is designed for that duty. Identify concentration, volume, controlled drain procedure and treatment before any release.
closure_document: PFD destination / chemical-drainage and treatment design

location: LG-102 and LG-103 transfer to LG-101; storm-water connection
observed: Both drain lagoons connect to a transfer route to LG-101, which has an overflow/bypass to storm water. No controlled release, dechlorination or water-quality acceptance function is shown.
required_action: Define gravity/pumped transfer and reverse-flow prevention from actual levels. Hold and dechlorinate hyperchlorination effluent to the approved discharge criterion before transfer/release. Confirm contaminated pump-hall water acceptance/treatment, transfer isolation and monitoring, lagoon/overflow capacity and authority approval for the storm-water interface.
closure_document: PFD treatment/release function / drainage P&ID / discharge approval

location: Pump/motor/lube-oil areas to PT-811 / LG-103
observed: Lube-oil heat-exchange equipment is shown and floor/pump/valve drainage joins LG-103. Treatment or separate containment of possible oil-contaminated water is unstated.
required_action: Confirm whether the actual pump/lube equipment can introduce oil into floor drains. If so, provide suitable containment/separation and controlled disposal before clean drainage/storm-water release; otherwise record the clean-drain basis. Do not assume every pump-hall drain automatically requires an oil separator.
closure_document: Drainage classification / OEM leakage data / treatment design

location: Referenced W-G-SS-017, W-M-SS-007 and N14054 typical P&IDs
observed: The cited specifications, reference P&IDs, vendor package P&IDs and detailed hydraulic/transient studies were not supplied with this five-sheet PDF.
required_action: Use the reviewed PFD as a functional baseline, then reconcile it with the actual project and package P&IDs, valve schedules and approved studies. This review cannot establish that every installed valve exists or verify the cited standard clauses, sizes, pressure classes or settings.

location: Band-3 scalability table and functional/TYP tags
observed: The Band-3 example table includes 100 MIGD, while the stated band definition places 100 MIGD in Band 2. Several repeated valves/vessels use a single functional or typical tag.
required_action: Label 100 MIGD as a boundary example or align the table with the band definition. Retain functional/TYP identification at PFD level if intended, but assign unique equipment and valve identities when the project P&IDs/schedules are issued. Do not count each typical symbol as a certified bill of materials.
closure_document: PFD editorial clarification / project tag schedule
